title: C Rule-255 decompress validates nothing: verbatim memcpy where Python and Rust decode_rule255 enforce validate_full_ipv6
description: Confirmed empirically by two independent codereview passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-njdx. lichen/subsys/schc/schc.c:151-165 copies Rule-255 payloads to out without any validation; Python decode_rule255 (headers.py:193 -> validate_full_ipv6) and Rust decode_rule255 (codec.rs:1444) run the full validator and reject. Demonstrated: ff + RH3(sl=1)+UDP with bad checksum -> C lichen_schc_decompress ret=76 payload copied, P/R reject; ff + IPv6 Fragment header packet -> C ret=60 accepted, P/R reject. The parity corpus has no malformed-category vector with rule_id 255 (all use 0-7), so this cannot be caught by the current gate. Impact: a C receiver admits on-air Rule255 frames that every Rust/Python peer rejects, and locally accepts packets the firmware's own compress gate rejects (asymmetric admission). Fix: run validate_ipv6_transport_lengths + the chain policy over the decoded payload in the C rule-255 decompress branch, then add shared malformed rule-255 compressed vectors (fragment header, bad checksum, non-RH3 routing) so the parity gate pins it. Related: project-LICHEN-worker6-prld covers Python/Rust Rule255 laxness; this is the C-side decode gap.
close_reason: Fixed by 5rvk (commit 6c618ddda6, this branch): schc_decompress's rule255 branch now calls the profile validate_payload hook (validate_ipv6_transport_lengths - structure + UDP checksums, no address policy) BEFORE the memcpy, so the bead's demo cases are rejected: ff + UDP bad checksum -> SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE from the checksum check (schc_helpers.c:530-531); ff + Fragment header -> rejected by validate_ipv6_header_chain (schc_helpers.c:445-447). Corpus gap the bead flagged (no rule255 malformed vectors) closed this round: rule255_rx_bad_checksum_malformed + rule255_rx_fragment_header_malformed added to test/vectors/schc_compression.json (category malformed, rule_id 255 - drives DECOMPRESS rejection in all three harnesses via check_malformed_compressed/decompress-packet/decode is_err), header regenerated (61 vectors, gen_vectors --check byte-identical). Verified on heft: C parity 61/61 (clang+ASan/UBSan), python test_vectors 780/780, rust shared_vectors 3/3. Reviewer independently confirmed attribution for both vectors (counterfactual: restoring the labeled byte makes each decompress OK; rejection sites traced per implementation - C hook/checksum/fragment checks, python headers.py:156-157/148-149, rust codec.rs:325-329/343-351) and confirmed positive controls exist (11 fallback-category rule255 round-trip vectors). 3x codereview: no P0-P2.
